correctness.rationale: A proper power self-overlaps, and distinct rotations of a word overlap at the cut; thus a code has at most one member per primitive rotation class. A nonprimitive weight-three word must be a triple repetition, giving exactly n/3 exceptions when 3 divides n and none otherwise. Dividing the primitive count by n gives the stated floor. For the proposed code every prefix starts at the first 1. A proper suffix either starts with 0, starts at the third 1 and has length at least m (so the competing prefix has at least two 1s), or starts at the second 1 and has length at least B (so the competing prefix has three 1s). This checks all ordered pairs, including self-pairs. The sum of B-a for 2≤a≤m is (m-1)(2n-3m)/2, which agrees with the bound in each residue modulo three; n=3 has only the bordered word 111. Equality proves that the displayed construction meets each primitive rotation class exactly once. This is an optimal family, not a classification of all optimal families. The frozen replay is check.py alongside RESULT.md, for lengths 3 through 30; it was inspected, not executed. The proof is all-length and does not depend on this check.
